rows.abstract: Amends Section 482 (a) of RA 7160 to read as follows: "SECTION 482. rows.abstract: "Public Land Utility Transport Act of 1996" Mandates operators of land utility vehicles to maintain their vehicles in good condition and to equip these with necessary devises  and accessories. Does not allow vehicles or buses which have been plyingfor 20 years to operate.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 1996-07-23

rows.author: A040
rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED SEVEN HUNDRED AND SIXTY, AS AMENDED BY CONTINUING THE BAREBOAT CHARTERING PROGRAM AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: "The present measure is in recognition of the growing need to accelerate the expansion and modernization of the shipping industry.  It proposes a continuing bareboat chartering program that would guarantee foreign exchange earnings for the country, enhance maritime employment, provide sufficient financial resources to acquire new tonnage to replace unecconomic and over-aged fleet and provide for a system of registry that is not too dependent on time-bound provisions but more focusedon long-term development of the industry as well as training of seamen and related professions"
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 1996-07-23

rows.author: A041
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING PUBLIC AND PRIVATE OFFICES AND COMMERCIAL ESTABLISHMENTS TO DISPLAY THE PHILIPPINE FLAG EVERYDAY, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: Mandates that the Philippine flag shall be conspicuously displayed in all public and private offices and commercial establishments everyday of the year. States that --- "SECTION 2. Any private person, natural or juridical, who shall vioalte the provision of Section 1 hereof shall be punished with imprisonment of not less than two (2) years nor more than six (6) years or a fine ranging from Twenty thousand Pesos (P20,000.00) to Fifty thousand pesos (P50,000.00) or both such fine and imprisonmentat the discretion of the court."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1996-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING SECTIONS 27 AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8045 AND SECTIONS 28, 29 AND 30 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7166 BY PROVIDING FOR COMELEC TABULATION OF MUNICIPAL AND CITY RETURNS FOR NATIONALLY ELECTED OFFICIALS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Seeks to do away with the provincial canvass for nationally elected oficials. Municipal and city returns shall be sent by the fastest and most reliable means of communication direct to COMELEC which will tabulate about 1,609 returns. Thus, each return will only be about 1/1,609 or .062% of the total votes cast. This will make tampering of returns more difficult because of the much bigger number of returns and city returns which would be about 142.
rows.status: Substituted by HB00168

rows.abstract: Seeks to --- (1) to recognize the importance of art and cultural development as guiding tool for the upliftment and formation of youth's values; (2) to provide mechanism in recognition and honoring the efforts of the youth for their artistic excellence and contribution to the community; and (3) to create opportunities for popularizing youth's artistic works and talents locally as well as internationally .

rows.author: B043
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A DEPARTMENT OF MARITIME AFFAIRS, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Department of Maritime Affairs Act" Rationale: However, to date the Philippine Marchant Marine, both domestic and international, is in a sad and sorry state. A very low priortiy has been given for maritime development by past administation and ourmaritime potential has never been dully exploited. There is therefore the most urgent need for the government to immediately focus on the growth and development requirements of our Maritime Industry in view of the great significance of the industry to total national development efforts and those requirements can only be effectively addressed by the establishment of a Department of Maritime Affairs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 1996-07-24

rows.author: A101
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING BONA-FIDE STUDENTS FARE DISCOUNTS IN LAND, AIR AND SEA TRANSPORTATION
rows.abstract: Provides for the following --- "SECTION 2. SCOPE AND COVERAGE - Upon approval of this Act, all types of public transportation, including but not limited to BUSES, JEEPNEYS, TRICYCLES, CALESAS, AIRPLANES, and SHIPS granted a franchise by government to operate, shall give TWENTY (20) PERCENT DISCOUNT on the basic fare to students." "SECTION 3. IDENTIFICATION CARDS - To avail of the student fare disccount a student upon boarding the public transport must show a duly issued identification card oreregistration form." "SECTION 4. PENALTIES - any public utility operator and/or driver who refuses to give a student fare discount shall suffer the indeterminate penalty of SIX YEARS in prison and a fine of TEN THOUSAND PESOS or both upon the discretiion of the Courts. Likewise, the operators franchise ti operate shall be revoked and the License to Drive of the driver cancelled."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 1996-07-24

rows.author: A101
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE TRADITIONAL AND ALTERNATIVE HEALTH CARE INSTITUTE TO ACCELERATE THE DEVELOPMENT OF TRADITIONAL AND ALTERNATIVE HEALTH CARE IN THE PHILIPPINES, PROVIDING FOR A TRADITIONAL AND ALTERNATIVE HEALTH CARE DEVELOPMENT FUND AND FOR OTHERPURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Traditional and Alternative Health Care Development Act of 1996" Seeks to --- (a) to encourage scientific research on and development of traditional and alternative health care systems, particualry those with direct impact on public health; (b) topromote and advocate the use of traditional and alternative health care modalities that have been proven safe, effective and consistent with government standdards on medical practices; (c) to formulate standards, guidelines and codes of ethical practice appropriate for the practice of traditional and alternative health care as well as in the manufacturem marketing and quality control of different traditional and alternative health care materials and product for approval and adoption by the approopriate governemnt agencies.
rows.status: Substituted by HB10070

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF MICROSCOPY CENTERS IN EVERY BARANGAY THROUGHOUT THE COUNTRY, THE ACQUISITION OF ADDITIONAL MICROSCOPES, THE EMPLOYMENT OF ADDITIONAL MICROSCOPISTS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Provides for the following --- "SECTION 1. There shall be established at least one microscopy center in every barangay throughout the country.  Each microscopy center shall be equipped with functional microscopes, which number shall not be less thanthat which is required to have a ratio of microscope for every 2,000 barangay population." "SECTION 2. Additional microscopists shall be employed to meet the manpower requirement for the full operation of all microscopy centers, subhect to the occupational standards and requirements set by the Department of Health for this function."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 1996-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED EIGTH HUNDRED SEVENTY SEVEN, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'PHILIPPINE NURSING LAW', AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale: "Thus, nurses today are required to have new skills, new knowledge and new attitudes and perspectives of their work as professionals. The Nursing Law of 1953, as amended, has to be revised and updated if only to reflect the new reality ofthe nursing profession, solve the problem that beset the professionals and truly make her a part of the health care team delivering quality patient care to the various health centers and institutions in the country."

rows.abstract: Seeks to reconcile Section 1 (c) of Presidential Decree No. 1829 and Art. 20 of the Revised Penal code with respect to those who commit a crime as mere accessory by harboring or concealing the escape of any person he knows, or has reasonable groundto believe or suspect, has committed any offence under existing penal laws in order to prevenet his arrest, prosecution and conviction.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND SECTION TWO HUNDRED TWENTY OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVEN THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991' AND FOR TOHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Provides that REAL PROPERTY CLASSIFIED AS RESIDENTIAL SHALL NOT BE REASSESSED MORE OFTENER THAT ONCE EVERY TEN YEARS AND AND THAT EACH PREASSESSMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED TWENTY PERCENT ON LAND AND TEN PERCEN ON BUILDINGS AND OTHER STRUCTURES; AND PROVIDED, FINALLY, THAT IN CASE OF VIOALTION OF THIS PROVISION, A PENALTY OF PERPETUAL DISQUALIFICATIO N TO HOLD PUBLIC OFFICE OR A FINE OF NOT EXCEEDING THREE HUNDRED THOUSAND PESOS OR BOTH DISQUALIFICATIO N AND FINE IN THE DISCRETION OF THE COURT, SHALLBE IMPOSED.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 1996-07-24

rows.abstract: Amends Section 17, subsection (c) of the LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE to read as follows: "SECTION 17. (c). [Notwithstandin g the provisions of subsection (b) hereof] Public Works and infrastructure projects and other facilities, programs and services funded by the National Government udner the Annual General Appropriations Act, other special laws, pertinent Executive Orders, and those wholly or partly funded from foreign sources, [are not] SHALL BE covered udner this section (.)" [except in those cases where the local government unit concerned is duly designated as the implementing agency for such projects, facilities, programs and services.]"
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 1996-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE ADDITIONAL AD VALOREM TAX ON IDLE LANDS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Ratioanale: "Raising the effective tax rate on idle and unproductive lands would hopefully, strengthen the government's urban and rural land reform programs.  The owners thereof would be constrained to utilize the land for proeductive purposes because of the additional tax burden. In case of agricultural lands, trees and other crops may be planted; in case of commercial and industrial lands, factories and other business establishments can be put up while in the case of residential lands, housing projects for the poor may be undertaken by the landowners thereof." States that --- "SECTION 236. Additional Ad Valorem Tax on Idle Lands. - A province or city, or a municipality within the Metropolitan Manila Area, may levy an annual tax on idle llands at the rate not exceeding [five percent (5%)] FIFTEEN PERCENT (15%) of the assessed value of the property which shal be in addition to the basic real property tax."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 1996-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXTENDING REGULAR BANKING HOURS TO EIGHT HOURS AND REGULAR BANKING DAYS TO SIX DAYS

rows.abstract: Provides for this --- "SECTION 1. Capability building Program.  The Local Government Academy shall develop and implement a regular capability building program for local executives, legislators and government employees. The program shall provide standardized courses in local administration for local executives including provincial governors, city mayors, municipal mayors and barangay chairmen; local legislation for local legislators including provincial board members, city councilors, municipalcouncilors and barangay councilors and the various technical areas of concern in local governance for local government employees."
